_comment: Stage-2 builder + run recipes for Yggdrasil, one entry per target.
Faithful to the showboat-verified DEMO.md. Read by both the `yggdrasil`
CLI (build/run subcommands) and Bifrost's shake-then-run mode.
Placeholders substituted at run time (all absolute paths):
{yggroot}   Yggdrasil repo root (holds yggdrasil.shen, KLambda/, builders/)
{outdir}    the shake output dir (kernel.kl + <prog>.kl + manifest)
{tmp}       a scratch dir for intermediate build tools
{shen_lua}/{shen_go}/{shen_rust}/{shenscript}/{shen_julia}/{shen_scheme}/
{shen_swift}/{shen_erl}/{shen_cl}/{shen_truffle}/{shen_c} sibling port repo roots;
default to {yggroot}/../<name>, overridable via the env var
named in each target's 'dir_env'.
Each target: 'build' is a list of steps (argv + optional cwd/env), run in
order; 'run' is the argv that executes the built artifact and prints to
stdout; 'needs' lists external tools that must be on PATH (else SKIP).
The Erlang target compiles the shaken slice to BEAM with shen-erl; scheme
compiles via kl->scheme; swift interprets the minimal slice directly.
The C target (shen-c) emits NativeFunction C + Makefile/CMakeLists and
links libshenc.a (option 5 rung 1; not eval_kl_object of the source).
A step whose argv[0] is '{yggdrasil}' is not a subprocess: it names one
of yggdrasil's own build helpers (main.go's internalSteps, also reachable
as `yggdrasil <name> ...` for debugging). They exist for the steps that
are LOGIC rather than a command line -- 'program-file' concatenates
kernel.kl, (shen.initialise) and the manifest's user files into one KL
stream -- so a target that needs one is still an entry in this file
rather than a runner hard-coded in Go.
'program_file' (substituted as {program_file}) says the run's stdin must
carry that file before anything else: it is how a runtime that reads its
PROGRAM from stdin is described as data. Declare it together with the
'stdin' fact below, which is what makes the consequences visible.
Facts inherited by every target that does not state its own.
loadBuilders() skips _-prefixed keys; prune.go's portReadsFor()
reads this block explicitly.
Fact provenance is three flat keys per fact:
<key>                the fact
<key>_source         where it was read from, or 'none'
<key>_checked_by     the test that fails when it drifts, or 'none'
A fact whose _checked_by is 'none' is DECLARED, never verified;
`yggdrasil contract --target T` prints which is which.
port_reads is the literal string "unknown", and that is the whole
point: only `go` has had its native reads read off a runtime, so for
every other target this repository does not know the answer. It used
to hold a 35-name conservative guess, which every undeclared target
inherited -- absence of a measurement wearing the shape of a fact.
A target that resolves to unknown is REFUSED by --prune-init (see
prune.go) and prints `port_reads  unknown` in `yggdrasil contract`.
Replace this with a real list on a target's own entry, with a source
and a checked_by, when someone measures one.
_default.port_reads_source: none: nobody has read this port's native global reads off its runtime. The previous value here was a conservative guess (go's five native reads plus every global the kernel's own defuns read in a full boot) presented as data for twelve ports that were never measured
_default.stdin_source: the default run contract: `yggdrasil run` and the parity gate hand the caller's bytes (or --stdin FILE) to the artifact's own stdin, and the artifact's program comes from its build
_default.stdin_checked_by: scripts/parity-gate.sh on tests/stdin-sum.shen: the fixture reads its stdin and prints a digest of it, so a port that did not receive those bytes fails the gate
_default.stdout_source: the default run contract: the artifact's stdout is the program's output and nothing else, which is what makes tests/<fixture>.expected comparable byte for byte
_default.stdout_checked_by: scripts/parity-gate.sh: every gated target's stdout is compared with the committed golden under canon()

go.port_reads_source: shen-go da55c5d kl/primitives.go (*stinput*, *stoutput*), kl/kernelfast.go nativeFn (shen.*lambdatable*) and primArityFast (*property-vector*), kl/prim.go ResolveHomePath (*home-directory*)
go.port_reads_checked_by: TestPruneInitGoArtifactStillRuns (prune_test.go) and the parity gate: the pruned go slice builds and prints fib.expected. One-directional: a name added here that go does not read makes the pruned slice keep a form it should not, and a name that go DOES read but this list omits breaks the run -- but a name removed from a list that is already a superset only prunes less, and nothing fails
go.native_overrides_source: shen-go da55c5d kl/kernelfast.go InstallKernelFast: every symbol rebound there (BindSymbolFunc / restoreCanonicalPrimitive / overridePrimitive / overrideNative)
go.native_overrides_checked_by: TestNativeOverridesMatchKernelFast (prune_test.go): parses InstallKernelFast in the sibling checkout and compares both ways, so a name added here and a name removed from here both fail
go.native_overrides_installed_after_source: shen-go da55c5d cmd/yggdrasil-build/main.go genMain: run(&e, "shen.initialise", ...) is emitted before runHelper("InstallKernelFast", ...), so the kernel's KL bodies run during boot and the natives replace them only afterwards
go.special_forms_source: shen-go da55c5d, derived as a class and not from a fixture's residue. `do` is syntactic: src/compiler.shen:6 `Env [do X Y] -> [$do (parse Env X) (parse Env Y)]`, the only parse head that is also a kernel defun. The other six are exactly the intersection of the `shenPrimitive` table (codegen/codegen.go:919-965) with kernel.kl's 687 defun names, each emitted by emitDirectPrimitive (codegen/codegen.go:888) as a bare Go call with no PrimFunc lookup, unconditionally for kernel chunks because cmd/yggdrasil-build/main.go:428 sets `cg.Sealed = true` before compiling them: `not` codegen.go:958 -> PrimNot, `symbol?` :960 -> PrimIsSymbol, `read-file-as-bytelist` :961 -> PrimReadFileAsByteList, `read-file-as-string` :962 -> PrimReadFileAsString, `variable?` :963 -> PrimIsVariable, `integer?` :964 -> PrimIsInteger. Which of the seven a given slice actually needs subtracted is a property of the program; the declaration is the port's whole class.

_comment: The shaken KL run directly on shen-go's bare KLambda VM (cmd/kl in
the same checkout the `go` target uses), no stage-2 compiler in
between. It is the most direct reading of the question trace-check
asks -- the claim under test is about the KL the shake WRITES -- and
the fallback when the `go` builder's own full-kernel compiler image
will not boot. `--target go` remains the compositional case that also
checks the backend.
This was a runner hard-coded in trace.go (klRunner) that borrowed the
`go` entry's dir_env at run time and was reachable from exactly one
subcommand. It is an entry here so that build, run, parity and
trace-check all reach it through the one data path, and so that what
is peculiar about it is DECLARED (stdin, stdout below) rather than
matched on the target's name in Go.
kl.stdin_source: shen-go cmd/kl/main.go: the VM reads its program from os.Stdin and takes no file argument, so the run feeds it {program_file} and whatever the caller sends on stdin arrives AFTER the program text, as further toplevel forms -- the program itself then reads EOF
kl.stdin_checked_by: TestStdinFactDrivesTheSkip and TestEvidencePossible (trace_test.go): trace-check refuses a fixture stdin on any target declaring this value, by name, before anything is shaken
kl.stdout_source: shen-go cmd/kl/main.go: the VM prints a numbered prompt and echoes each toplevel form's value, and ends the program by recovering a panic and printing the dump, so the program's output is EMBEDDED in a transcript that also carries goroutine addresses and is not byte-stable across two boots of the same program
kl.stdout_checked_by: TestCheckGolden/kl-containment (trace_test.go) and TestTranscriptTargetIsComparedByContainment (parity_test.go): a golden is checked by containment in the transcript -- on both the vs-truth and the two-boot leg -- which is the strongest thing assertable there

_comment: Two mutually exclusive steps, selected on the manifest's needs-eval.
ShenScript's default mode is fully self-contained but refuses
needs-eval=true (an eval-capable slice needs the compiler in the
artifact); --linked can carry the compiler but imports lib/ from the
ShenScript checkout, so it is NOT portable off the build machine.
Passing --linked unconditionally would trade a loud failure on one
program for a quiet portability regression on every eval-free one.
